landing_plan.rule: A joint landing plan lands the moving side's airborne aircraft (its own and those of minors it controls and moves): each lands ashore within its remaining range or on a carrier seat in a zone the carrier is in or can still reach this phase; each carrier ends in one zone; a sailing carrier launches its own aircraft where its route begins; an aircraft on a carrier that can still fly ashore frees its seat. The shortfall counts the aircraft that no such plan lands. No move may raise it, and a flying aircraft must itself keep a landing; with a complete plan this is the complete-plan rule. Combat Movement ends once the carriers stand where they land every aircraft a plan can land (RB 9.3), and the rest are lost as it ends; Noncombat Movement ends only when the mover's patrols can land as the carriers stand. Other nations' patrols are lost by RB 9.3.1.
landing_plan.stranded_aircraft_lost: counts aircraft removed as Combat Movement ends because no landing remains; only dice or another nation's turn leave any
landing_plan.remaining_gap: A war declared during Combat Movement, by the mover or by a neutral answering a peaceful entry where a carrier's route ends, can change which zones aircraft may enter or hold a carrier in battle; no plan check follows it
landing_plan.conservative_cases: Carrier routes count only if they meet no unfriendly unit before their last zone, and a ship that combat-moved into Enemy units is treated as staying for their battle
landing_plan.copying: Flights, landings, attacks and naval air attacks preview the aircraft's end on the position itself; carrier routes and engagements test a copy only when landings are at stake; patrol starts test a copy

design.transport: per-thread 8 MB shared-memory buffer and pipe; the coordinator batches per alliance model

setup_probes.note: opening rounds only; chose the setup, not compared with complete runs

run.whole_game_average_note: slots / mean game time, as the CPU-only figure is computed; it counts the faster last games, so it overstates a long run

cpu_only_reference.whole_game_average_note: no record over time was kept, so the rate with all ten playing is unknown

comparison.one_batch_note: a batch's rate depends on its size (10 and 32 games), so the long-run ratios compare fairly
comparison.limits: No learning updates and no strength measurement; same seeds do not force identical games; the runs used different seeds (1951-1960, 1951-1982), PyTorch 2.11.0 and 2.14.0, and engines 873058a and b89e86d, one rule change apart at about the same cost per call
